Thanks for the draft DPA. A few items that are blocking procurement review on our side:

1) Notification timing: we typically require a 48-hour notification window for confirmed breaches affecting personal data (some exceptions for investigation allowed). Can you confirm Redwood is comfortable with 48 hours?

2) Subprocessor obligations: we need explicit language that your subprocessors must notify Redwood within 24 hours of becoming aware of an incident that impacts our data, and that Redwood will in turn notify us in the stated timeframe. Also need visibility into the subprocessors map and a commitment to provide evidence custody details.

3) Evidence custody & forensic access: we need assurance on custody chain-of-evidence, temporary forensic access rights for our appointed third-party forensics vendor, and a timeline for transferring relevant forensic snapshots/evidence (we've requested 5 business days in some agreements).

4) Cross-border assistance: if evidence or logs require transfer for investigation, we need cooperation and any required assistance for lawful transfer.

Can you send a proposed set of clause language (redline) we can review? Procurement would also like your most recent SOC 2 (redacted ok).

John —

Appreciate the clear list. We've drafted proposed language below and attached a redline to the DPA for your review. High-level responses:

- Notification timing: our standard is 72 hours for confirmed security incidents that affect customer personal data; we allow an earlier notification if the investigation can confirm material impact sooner. We understand Finarya's position on 48 hours; willing to discuss narrowing to 48 hours for "confirmed" incidents where scope is quickly established, with a fast-update cadence during investigation.

- Subprocessors: we obligate subprocessors by contract to report incidents to Redwood within 24 hours; Redwood will report to customers per the DPA windows. We can add explicit chain-of-custody reporting requirements and a subprocessor contact roster (redacted).

- Evidence custody & forensic access: we propose a forensic handover window of up to 5 business days for initial snapshot and a 14-day preservation period while parties agree on the scope and extraction method. We can allow a vetted third-party forensic vendor access under an NDA and supervision model.

- Cross-border assistance: Redwood will cooperate with lawful transfer requests and assist with export controls/technical handover; we may require lawful process or data processing addenda for certain jurisdictions.

Proposed clause (excerpt):
"Redwood shall notify Customer of any confirmed incident affecting Customer Personal Data without undue delay and, in any event, no later than seventy-two (72) hours after Redwood has determined that a security incident affecting Customer Personal Data has occurred. For incidents where Redwood can confirm material impact within forty-eight (48) hours, Redwood shall notify Customer within forty-eight (48) hours and provide initial mitigation steps. Redwood shall require its Subprocessors to notify Redwood within twenty-four (24) hours of learning of any incident that may affect Customer Personal Data and to provide chain-of-custody documentation for any preserved evidence. Redwood will provide Customer (or Customer’s designated third-party forensics vendor) with read-only access to preserved snapshots under a mutual NDA and reasonable supervision within five (5) business days of a written request."

I've attached: FINARYA_DPA_redline_20260524.docx (our redline) and a template evidence-chain workbook. Ben / Marissa — flagged for legal/ops review; Ben, please confirm any SLA implications or risks.

Thanks,

Evelyn —

Quick comments from legal/ops:

- 72/48 compromise looks reasonable operationally, but we should scope "confirmed incident" precisely (e.g., confirmed exfiltration or unauthorized access to Customer Personal Data as defined in Section X). Otherwise we risk noisy alerts that create SLA pressure.

- For subprocessors: the 24-hour inbound notification requirement is fine, but subprocessors often report to us before we can validate — we should add language that allows Redwood to triage and confirm before the customer-facing notification goes out (we still meet the customer's timing requirement once confirmed).

- Forensic handover: 5 business days for a preserved snapshot is operationally achievable for most cases; full exports may take longer depending on data volume and region. Suggest adding a "reasonable efforts" qualifier and an explicit export cost clause if large-volume forensic exports are requested.

- Escalation: propose adding an explicit senior-responsible-person contact and a weekly cadence during the first 30 days for major incidents.

I'll send a legal redline with tightened definitions. Irene, can you confirm any compliance/legal constraints on cross-border transfer assistance?

-Ben

Evelyn / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of follow-ups from procurement/security:

- We really need the customer-facing notification to be within 48 hours for confirmed incidents; the proposed language that allows Redwood to "confirm" before notifying introduces ambiguity and could push the clock out. Can we state: Redwood shall provide Customer with initial notification within forty-eight (48) hours of Redwood becoming aware of a security incident that reasonably appears to affect Customer Personal Data, with a follow-up investigation summary within seven (7) calendar days.

- Subprocessor notification: we require Redwood to provide the identity of the subprocessor(s) involved within forty-eight (48) hours of confirming the incident and a written statement of the subprocessor chain-of-custody within five (5) business days.

- Forensics: the 5 business day snapshot window is fine; however, we want the option to request expedited export at Redwood's cost if we can justify material business impact.

If you can accept those tightening edits, procurement will advance the DPA. We can sign a mutual NDA for vendor forensic access.

-John

John —

Thanks — we can accept the tightened language with a small set of guardrails to allow operational triage:

- Agreed: initial customer-facing notification within forty-eight (48) hours of Redwood becoming aware of a security incident that reasonably appears to affect Customer Personal Data. We will include a one-paragraph initial summary and a follow-up investigation summary within seven (7) calendar days, then weekly status updates for the first 30 days.

- Subprocessor identity: Redwood will provide the identity of involved Subprocessors within forty-eight (48) hours of confirming their involvement and will provide chain-of-custody documentation within five (5) business days. Redwood will include an option to mark sensitive contact details as redacted where regulatory restrictions apply, but will provide sufficient detail to support Customer's forensics.

- Expedited exports: Redwood will make reasonable efforts to accommodate expedited evidence exports; for large volume exports that materially impact Redwood operations, we may charge a one-time fee (to be defined) or propose a mutually agreed export plan.
